origin_derivations.WT-1: Session.init/1 is the only backend assignment (options.backend, default HTTP.WebTransport.Transport.QUIC). New sites migrate (202), handle_message (203) and acknowledge (204) call that retained module after function_exported?/3 checks. backend_or_invalid_state/2 (205) and finish_send/3 (206) invoke only the local closures built in handle_call/3 around the same retained backend; close moved to cleanup_backend/2 (ID 159) and the send-close/abort closures moved to finish_send/3 (IDs 163/164). The sole library backend now opens a real exclusive HTTP3 ConnectionOwner with a Quic.Cleanup.new/1 descriptor, literal webtransport session options and caller ssl keywords validated by SSL.QUIC.Config; its stream/datagram/migration bodies are literal ConnectionOwner and Cleanup calls covered by H3-1/H3-2/Q1.
origin_derivations.HTTP-1_HTTP-4: Alt-Svc keeps tls_backend nil only until the TCP fallback pins it through TLSBackend.resolve/1, which accepts only ExSSL. HTTP/3 options lift ex_ssl reference identity into QUIC ssl data. SocketClient transport/protocol selectors and the H3 handler are unchanged; 12 SocketClient sites move.
origin_derivations.HTTP-9: WebSocket over HTTP/3 leaves tls_backend unresolved; Runtime.Options rejects any explicit backend for HTTP/3 and the HTTP1 selector still maps only :ex_ssl. Seven WebSocket sites move with unchanged expressions.
origin_derivations.HTTP-2: The nine RequestLifecycle worker producers are unchanged in number and kind.

follow_up_changes.change: ConnectionOwner.terminate/2 now runs QuicHttp3.Session.close/1 under guarded/4 on an orderly :normal stop of a ready or draining owner, then retires the cleanup lease; the :http3_retire handler no longer retires before stopping, so the close is admitted first (RFC 9114 section 5.2, H3_NO_ERROR).
follow_up_changes.dispatch_review: No dynamic dispatch added or moved: the new calls are the literal Session.close/1 inside the existing guarded/4 closure invocation, and the file holds no reviewed occurrence. Session.close/1 reaches only the already reviewed retained session.transport close and cleanup operations (H3-1).

follow_up_changes.change: HTTP.WebSocket.Connection.finish/4 retires a cleanly closed HTTP/3 attempt with RequestLifecycle.retire_owner/1 before detach/1 instead of aborting it, so the connection owner survives to close with H3_NO_ERROR.
follow_up_changes.dispatch_review: No dynamic dispatch added or moved: the new orderly_retire/2 calls only the literal RequestLifecycle.retire_owner/1 and is placed after every reviewed occurrence; the seven HTTP-9 occurrences keep their lines and functions.

follow_up_changes.change: ConnectionOwner marks itself :retiring when the watchdog, attempt tracker or creator goes DOWN, so terminate/2 skips the graceful close of the already retired connection; graceful_close/2 now also requires that no request remains, so a stop that abandons live requests through fail_all/2 keeps the previous retire/abort path instead of claiming H3_NO_ERROR.
follow_up_changes.dispatch_review: No dynamic dispatch added or moved: the change is a lifecycle field update and a map_size/1 guard; the file holds no reviewed occurrence.

follow_up_changes.change: An extended CONNECT request whose response stream finished is marked done? and no longer counts as live, so graceful_close/2 still sends H3_NO_ERROR after a WebTransport session closed by a compliant peer; any other remaining request keeps suppressing it.
follow_up_changes.dispatch_review: No dynamic dispatch added or moved: the change adds a request map field, a put_in/2 update and an Enum.any?/2 over the request map; the file holds no reviewed occurrence.
